description: Symbolic molecular representation and computation: building molecules from names, SMILES or InChI, querying properties, drawing 2D and 3D structures, substructure matching and modification, and balancing chemical reactions.

tools.name: Molecule
tools.description: Represents a molecule, constructed from a chemical name, SMILES or InChI string, an entity, or explicit atoms and bonds. It carries connectivity, stereochemistry and optional 3D coordinates. It is the central object for all chemistry functions.
tools.notes: Entity["Chemical", "Aspirin"] and ChemicalData names can be converted into Molecule objects directly.

tools.name: MoleculeValue
tools.description: Computes properties of a molecule such as molar mass, formula, count of rings, hydrogen bond donors or topological descriptors. A list of property names returns several at once. Use it as the general query function for molecular data.
tools.notes: MoleculeValue["Properties"] lists everything that can be computed.

tools.name: MoleculeProperty
tools.description: Represents a molecular property symbolically, so it can be passed around, applied to atoms or bonds, and used inside patterns. It is what MoleculeValue accepts as a property specification. Use it to build reusable property queries.

tools.name: MoleculePlot
tools.description: Draws a 2D structure diagram of a molecule, with options for atom labels, highlighting and layout. Substructures can be highlighted by pattern. Use it for publication figures and for verifying that a structure parsed correctly.

parameters.name: AtomLabels
parameters.description: How atoms are labelled, e.g. Automatic, "Name", or explicit rules.

tools.name: MoleculePlot3D
tools.description: Renders a molecule in three dimensions using ball-and-stick, spacefill or wireframe styles. Coordinates are generated if the molecule does not already have them. Use it for conformational visualization and presentations.
tools.notes: MoleculeModify[mol, "AddCoordinates3D"] generates coordinates explicitly when they are needed for further computation.

tools.name: MoleculeGraph
tools.description: Converts a molecule into a Graph whose vertices are atoms and edges are bonds. The full graph-analysis toolkit then becomes available. Use it for ring perception, connectivity analysis and graph-theoretic descriptors.

tools.name: MoleculePattern
tools.description: Represents a substructure pattern for matching within molecules, given by SMARTS or by atoms and bonds with wildcards. It is the chemical analogue of a pattern object. Use it for functional-group searching and reaction site identification.

tools.name: MoleculeContainsQ
tools.description: Tests whether a molecule contains a given substructure pattern, returning True or False. It performs proper subgraph isomorphism with chemical semantics. Use it for filtering compound libraries by functional group.

tools.name: FindMoleculeSubstructure
tools.description: Finds occurrences of a substructure pattern in a molecule and returns the matching atom indices. All matches can be requested rather than just the first. Use it to locate and then modify specific sites.

tools.name: MoleculeSubstructureCount
tools.description: Counts how many times a substructure pattern occurs in a molecule. It is faster than enumerating all matches when only the count matters. Use it for descriptor calculation and library screening.

tools.name: MoleculeModify
tools.description: Applies a named transformation to a molecule, such as adding or removing hydrogens, generating 3D coordinates, replacing substructures or canonicalizing. It returns a new molecule. Use it to prepare structures for computation or display.

tools.name: MoleculeAlign
tools.description: Aligns one molecule's 3D coordinates onto another's by minimizing the difference between corresponding atoms. It is the chemical analogue of point-set registration. Use it to compare conformers and docking poses.

tools.name: MoleculeEquivalentQ
tools.description: Tests whether two molecules represent the same chemical species, comparing connectivity and optionally stereochemistry. It handles different but equivalent input representations. Use it for deduplication of compound sets.

tools.name: MoleculeFreeQ
tools.description: Tests whether a molecule does not contain a given substructure pattern. It is the logical complement of MoleculeContainsQ. Use it for exclusion filters in compound screening.

tools.name: MoleculeDraw
tools.description: Opens an interactive structure editor in which a molecule can be drawn or modified by hand, returning the resulting Molecule object. It is useful for sketching structures that would be awkward to write as SMILES. The editor runs inside the notebook front end.
tools.notes: Requires the notebook front end; the returned value is an ordinary Molecule usable in computations.

tools.name: MoleculeRecognize
tools.description: Recognizes a chemical structure drawn in an image and returns the corresponding Molecule object. It performs optical chemical structure recognition. Use it to digitize structures from papers and scanned documents.

tools.name: ConnectedMoleculeQ
tools.description: Tests whether a molecule consists of a single connected component rather than several separate species. Salts and mixtures give False. Use it to validate input before computing properties that assume one species.
tools.notes: ConnectedMoleculeComponents splits a disconnected molecule into its separate species.

tools.name: ChemicalReaction
tools.description: Represents a chemical reaction symbolically, with reactant and product species and optional stoichiometric coefficients. It can be balanced, analyzed and displayed. Use it for stoichiometry and reaction bookkeeping.

tools.name: ReactionBalance
tools.description: Finds stoichiometric coefficients that balance a chemical reaction, returning the balanced reaction. Unbalanceable reactions return a failure. Use it for stoichiometry problems and reaction validation.

tools.name: ChemicalInstance
tools.description: Represents a specific physical sample of a chemical species with a given amount, phase or concentration. It connects abstract molecules to quantities usable in stoichiometric and thermodynamic computations. Use it in reaction and mixture calculations.

tools.name: ChemicalConvert
tools.description: Converts between chemical representations such as Molecule objects, SMILES, InChI, formulas and entities. It is the general-purpose translation function for chemical identifiers. Use it when integrating with external chemistry tools.

tools.name: ChemicalFormula
tools.description: Represents a chemical formula symbolically, as a count of each element rather than a full connectivity structure. It supports arithmetic and comparison used in stoichiometry. Use it when only composition matters.

tools.name: AtomList
tools.description: Returns the list of atoms in a molecule, optionally filtered by element or by an atom property. Atoms come back as Atom objects carrying their element and index. Use it for per-atom analysis and labelling.

tools.name: BondList
tools.description: Returns the bonds of a molecule, optionally filtered by bond type or by the elements they connect. Bonds are given as Bond objects with atom indices and order. Use it for connectivity analysis and bond-level descriptors.

tools.name: MoleculeName
tools.description: Returns a chemical name for a molecule, such as its IUPAC or common name. Several naming conventions are available. Use it to label structures and to present results readably.
